back: Fraction of test behaviours for which an attack elicited a policy-violating output according to a judge; depends on behaviours, attack, query budget and judge.
Interval for a proportion k/n: centre (p + z^2/2n)/(1+z^2/n), half-width z/(1+z^2/n) * sqrt(p(1-p)/n + z^2/4n^2). Stays inside [0,1].
Not zero risk: with 0 of 50 the 95% Wilson upper bound is about 7.1%.
Fraction of behaviours broken within k queries; non-decreasing in k; always report the budget.
Static: fixed attacks. Adaptive: attacker knows the defence and picks the best; report the union over attacks.

front: Sample size for a rate estimate
back: n ~ z^2 p(1-p) / h^2 for half-width h (385 for p = 0.5, h = 0.05).
Long-context attack with many in-context examples; success follows a power law in the number of shots and shares a mechanism with benign in-context learning.
Safety filters operate on tokens or meaning; the model can read shapes or encodings the filter does not recognise. Reading ability and vulnerability correlate.
An attacker model proposes prompts, sees replies and a judge's score and refines; needs only query access.
Fine-tuned model labelling inputs/outputs against a hazard taxonomy; can sit before, after or around the model; needs per-deployment false-positive checks.
Probes generate test inputs, detectors score outputs, harnesses run the pairs and report; static probes age as models are patched.
Direct: the user supplies hostile text. Indirect: it sits in retrieved or tool content that the application feeds to the model.

front: Three delivery routes of indirect injection
back: Retrieval (RAG), inbox/document workflows, and tool outputs.
Label content by trust, propagate labels, require ratification before side effects triggered by untrusted content; containment over prevention.
Private-data access + untrusted-content exposure + external communication. Removing any one breaks the exfiltration chain.
